title: A finite victory over de Bruijn-Erdős in interval discrepancy
summary: We study a finite form of the classical interval discrepancy problem. Starting from the unit interval, one repeatedly splits an existing interval into two until $n$ intervals have been produced. The discrepancy of such a process is the maximum, over all intermediate stages, of the ratio between the longest interval and the shortest interval. A theorem of de Bruijn and Erdős from 1949 shows that this ratio must approach $2$ as $n\to\infty$, and they give a sharp construction achieving this bound.
